# Phase 6 — alert levels and thresholds

*Generated by `hydrocascade realtime` on 2026-09-24.*

## Four levels, keyed to a unit's own history — Doc 09 §2.1-§2.2

| Level | Meaning | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | background conditions | below the unit's 95th percentile |
| Watch | conditions developing | 95th – 99th |
| Warning | elevated, action advisable | 99th – 99.9th |
| Emergency | severe | above 99.9th |

**Why percentiles of the unit's own record, not an absolute intensity.** A steep thin-soiled hillside above Mundakkai and a gentle slope near the coast differ in background intensity by orders of magnitude. An absolute threshold would alarm permanently in one place and never in the other. Scoring each unit against its own 2018–2023 distribution makes units comparable and makes the alert sayable in words: *conditions here are more extreme than 99.9% of days on record for this location.*

## Thresholds are optimised, not chosen — Doc 09 §2.3

`Cost = C_miss × missed events + C_FA × false alarms`, swept over a grid on the **validation period only**.

| cost ratio (miss : false alarm) | threshold | hit rate | false-alarm rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1:1 | 0.0001901 | 0.000 | 0.028 |
| 5:1 ← recommended default | 0.0001901 | 0.000 | 0.028 |
| 20:1 | 0.0001901 | 0.000 | 0.028 |

**We do not choose the cost ratio.** Doc 09 §2.3: *"That is a policy decision belonging to a disaster management authority, not to a student project. We supply the trade-off curve and a recommended default at 5:1, and we say so."* The curve is `figures/leadtime_vs_falsealarm.png`, which Doc 09 §2.4 calls the most operationally meaningful figure in the project — more so than any accuracy number.

## Persistence and hysteresis — Doc 09 §2.5

A level is raised only after **2 consecutive updates** at or above it, and lowered only after **4 consecutive updates** below. The asymmetry is deliberate: staying alert slightly too long is cheap, standing down slightly too early is not.

**Measured cost on the Wayanad roll:** lead time falls from nan h to nan h, a cost of nan h. That is the honest price of not flapping, and Doc 09 §2.5 requires it to be reported rather than absorbed quietly.

## What a level does **not** mean

A Warning is not a prediction that a landslide will happen. It is a statement that conditions at this unit are in the top 1% of its own record. Over a long enough period, 1% of days will reach it without anything happening — which is why the false-alarm rate is reported beside every lead time, and why the negative-control experiment in `reports/phase5_backtest.md` exists.
